Surrey 55+ homes for sale: condos and townhomes in age-restricted and retirement communities. Rules differ by building, so read the strata bylaws and the age rules before you offer. Condos and townhomes in Surrey are one line in the monthly reports.
55+ homes you can buy in Surrey

Surrey's 55+ homes come in several legal forms and are spread across South Surrey, Newton, Cloverdale, Fleetwood and Whalley: strata condos and townhouse complexes, one membership complex, pad-rent manufactured-home parks and one bare-land strata. Each row says which kind it is and how its 55+ rule is evidenced. Anything a source does not state is marked unconfirmed.

items.t: The City of Surrey names seven communities: City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey and Whalley. A city-wide 55+ search has to be run community by community — there is no single Surrey 55+ district.

Health care: Surrey Memorial Hospital, 13750 96 Ave (City Centre), serves most of the city; Peace Arch Hospital, 15521 Russell Avenue, White Rock, serves South Surrey; the Surrey-Newton Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 6830 King George Blvd.

blocks.text: Looks like a Surrey 55+ building but is not

items.t: Breakaway Bays — 1840 160 St (King George Corridor as listing data places it): A direct source conflict — not verified as 55+ on this evidence.
Ocean Park Village — 12928 17 Ave / 12915 16 Ave (Ocean Park, South Surrey): Read its bylaws before counting it.

Glenwood Village Heights — 6875 121 St (West Newton): The trap beside a real 55+ complex: listings for this complex (NWS3423, built 1991–1992) state "NO AGE RESTRICTIONS." The 55+ complex is Glenwood Village at 7156 121 St (NWS2768).
Highgrove — 15055 20 Ave (Sunnyside Park, South Surrey): Its own listing states "no age restrictions."

Crispen Bays — 7790 King George Blvd, and Crestway Bays — 8220 King George Blvd (East Newton): Manufactured-home parks listed by a park directory as all-ages; Crestway listings describe a "family-oriented" park. Not 55+.

Abbey Road — 15885 / 15875 84 Ave (Fleetwood Tynehead): A building directory records pets and rentals allowed with restrictions and no age restriction listed — not verified as 55+ despite the seniors-suggesting form.

Cedars at Panorama Ridge — 6811 135A St (Newton): Registered in the Assisted Living Registry as class SU (supportive recovery), not a seniors (SN) residence — not 55+ seniors housing despite the name.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Surrey

items.t: Membership complexes are neither strata nor freehold purchase in the usual sense: Sullivan Mews' own listings state it is a membership, not a strata, and that mortgages are not possible — financing, resale and transfer rules come from the membership documents, not the Strata Property Act.

Secondary suites (settled position): under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, one secondary suite may be permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite, and a suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area.

Short-term rentals in Surrey: under 90 consecutive days per patron counts as short-term; only the owner may host, the owner must live at the property as their primary residence, tenants cannot run one, and a business licence at $358 per year is required before operating — strata bylaws are a separate, building-level check on top.

blocks.text: Good to know about 55+ homes in Surrey

items.t: Two complexes on one Newton street carry almost the same name and opposite age rules: Glenwood Village (7156 121 St, NWS2768) is 55+; Glenwood Village Heights (6875 121 St, NWS3423) advertises "NO AGE RESTRICTIONS." A name-filtered condo or townhouse alert will mix them — the strata plan number is the reliable separator.

A care-sounding name in Newton is a recovery residence, not seniors housing: Cedars at Panorama Ridge (6811 135A St) is class SU (supportive recovery) in the provincial Assisted Living Registry — Surrey's clearest example of why a name or "seniors" marketing language is never a substitute for the registry class or the filed bylaw.

Surrey's 55+ supply comes in four legal forms, and a condo search shows only one of them. Strata complexes are the bulk; Sullivan Mews is a membership with no strata lot and, per its own listings, no conventional mortgage; three manufactured-home parks are pad-rent under park tenancy law, not strata law; and Sea Ridge Bays is a bare-land strata where you own the lot. The form decides financing, documents and exit before the floor plan matters.

Most of Surrey's 55+ strata complexes were built between 1986 and 2000. Fleetwood Gardens (2005) and The Greens at Douglas (2012–2013) are the newer exceptions, so a buyer who only searches the older South Surrey and Newton corridors never sees the city's newest 55+ stock.

faq.q: Is Surrey a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In September 2026 houses in Surrey had a sales ratio of 8%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market, and condos and townhomes 7%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many 55+ homes are for sale in Surrey?
faq.a: The listing feed on this page shows what is active now, and the number changes daily. Ask Jared and he will send you the 55+ homes in Surrey that match what you want.

faq.q: Can Jared alert me when 55+ homes come up in Surrey?
faq.a: Yes. Tell him the area, price range and must-haves and he will alert you the day a match is listed.

faq.q: Where can I see all Surrey homes?
faq.a: The Surrey homes for sale page covers every home type, and the Surrey market stats page has the monthly figures.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: The monthly SnapStats reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so the monthly counts here include both. The boards’ benchmark prices are published separately for apartments and townhomes.

faq.q: Do both of us have to be 55?
faq.a: Provincially, a younger spouse or partner of a qualifying resident is exempt in any case — confirm the building's bylaw in its Form B.

faq.q: Is Sullivan Mews a cheap way into a Surrey "condo"?
faq.a: It is not a condo and not a strata: its own listings state the purchase is a membership, that mortgages are not possible, with a 55+ age restriction, no smoking, 1 small pet and a maximum of 2 occupants. Read the membership documents before pricing it against strata units.

faq.q: How does Sea Ridge Bays differ from the three parks?
faq.a: You own the lot. Sea Ridge Bays is a bare-land strata — title recorded as Freehold Strata, listings stating "NO PAD FEES" and a monthly strata fee ($210 in the listings checked, including water) instead of pad rent — so strata law, including the 55+ bylaw and its provincial exemptions, governs instead of the MHPTA. Its listings also state "Council Approval Required," a strata-side wording a park buyer will not meet in a pad-rent park, where the equivalent step is the park owner's assignment consent.
There is no Surrey-wide pet rule for 55+ housing.

faq.q: Is a "White Rock" seniors residence actually in Surrey?
faq.a: Sometimes. Amica White Rock (15333 16 Ave) and Whitecliff (15501 16 Ave) are at Surrey civic addresses despite the name and the border marketing, and Peace Arch Hospital itself is in White Rock. The civic address, not the brand name, decides which city's bylaws and tax regime apply — White Rock is a separate municipality with its own zoning and OCP bylaws.

faq.q: Why do so few 55+ listings show up in a condos-only search?
faq.a: Form, not price. Most of Surrey's 55+ strata complexes are townhouse complexes, which a condos-only feed excludes by type, and the membership complex, the manufactured-home parks and Sea Ridge Bays also sit outside a strata-condo feed. The 55+ condo-form supply is five buildings: Fleetwood Gardens, Carriage House, Semiahmoo Estates, 13965 16 Ave and the apartment section of Chelsea Gardens.

faq.q: How many 55+ complexes are there in Surrey?
faq.a: The table above names every complex verified so far, by community. A single Surrey total would depend on how you treat the complexes whose 55+ rule is stated in listings but not yet confirmed from the strata bylaws, which the table marks as listing-stated. Confirm any building's bylaw in its Form B before relying on it.
